title: Find your way around a repository
summary: A GitHub repository page has areas for code and collaboration. Start with its README, then inspect the files and recent changes.
introduction: A GitHub repository page has areas for code and collaboration. Start with its README, then inspect the files and recent changes. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain find your way around a repository
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A GitHub repository page has areas for code and collaboration. Start with its README, then inspect the files and recent changes.

blocks.code:
Code: files and README
Issues: problems and ideas
Pull requests: proposed code changes
Actions: configured automated runs
blocks.title: Find your way around a repository

blocks.text: Each area answers a different question. To understand what a project does, the README is usually the best starting point.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose where you would look for a proposed spelling fix.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A public repository can still contain code that is unsafe to run; read setup steps before using them.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
